title: Normalization Factor Explorer
description: A fixed example spectrum rescaled live by three FFT normalization conventions against a pinned axis, with forward, inverse, and round-trip factors displayed.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
FFT
Numerical Conventions

learningObjectives: Calculate the forward factor for each convention at a given N
Demonstrate that scaling does not affect round-trip correctness
Recognize convention mismatch when comparing implementations
prerequisites: The DFT produces a magnitude per bin
Forward and inverse transforms as a pair

simulationModel.modelType: Display-only rescaling of a fixed spectrum
equations: forward_factor * inverse_factor * N = 1 for every convention
assumptions: A single fixed underlying spectrum is the source of truth
Only the first 16 bins are displayed
limitations: Does not model the inverse transform itself; the round-trip claim is stated rather than computed here

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Same-data-different-display comparison on a pinned axis
keyQuestions: Does any convention change the underlying signal?
Why do the conventions differ less at small N?
commonMisconceptions: That a magnitude difference between libraries implies a bug
That one convention is more correct than the others
assessmentOpportunities: Infer two libraries' conventions from their reported peak magnitudes
